findings.title: An invalid user URL in the config now stops startup with a raw ValidationError traceback instead of a friendly error
findings.problem: The new validator raises ValueError for user-editable values such as a non-http scheme, a link-local or metadata IP, or a malformed URL. It does this even for disabled instances. Pydantic turns that into a ValidationError, and nothing catches it. ensure_config (triggarr/config.py:370-373) only catches TOMLDecodeError and UnicodeDecodeError. Its docstring (config.py:344-345) says ValidationError is left to propagate because it means a schema bug. startup.py:192 calls ensure_config with no handler. So a hand-edited triggarr.toml with, for example, url = "radarr:7878" on a disabled instance used to load and now crashes the daemon at startup with an uncaught traceback through asyncio.run. It never reaches the friendly loguru error-and-exit path used for corrupt TOML. The rejection is intended (see the docstring). The problem is that the failure is unhandled.
findings.fix_hint: in ensure_config, catch pydantic.ValidationError from load_settings and log a friendly message naming the bad instance URL, then call sys.exit(1), like _log_corrupt_config_and_exit does
findings.why_it_matters: Users who upgrade with a stale or hand-edited config get a crash loop and a stack trace, not a clear message saying which instance URL to fix.

members.title: Config model layer now depends on the web presentation package for URL validation
members.problem: Before this diff, triggarr/models/ was a leaf layer. models/config.py and models/arr.py import only stdlib, pydantic and pydantic_settings, while triggarr/web/routes.py and triggarr/web/middleware.py import models.config. The new validator reverses that direction: it imports triggarr.web.validation, the web UI's form-input helper module, into the config model that the scheduler, engine, db, state and startup modules all load. The function-local import is a sign the author expected a cycle risk. There is no actual cycle today, because validation.py imports only stdlib and web/__init__.py is empty, but nothing enforces that.
source_window: Raises ValueError on violation so Pydantic surfaces a ValidationError.
members.why_it_matters: If anyone later adds an import of triggarr.models.config (or anything FastAPI-related) to web/validation.py or web/__init__.py, config loading will hit a circular import or pull web dependencies into every non-web consumer of the config model.
members.fix_hint: Move the SSRF URL validators (validate_arr_url, validate_arr_url_config, BLOCKED_HOSTS, _BLOCKED_NETWORKS) to a layer-neutral module, e.g. triggarr/url_safety.py, and re-export from web/validation.py. Then use a top-level import in config.py.

members.title: Config-load SSRF check can be bypassed with numeric or trailing-dot host forms that resolve to cloud metadata (data exposure)
members.problem: validate_arr_url_config (triggarr/web/validation.py:150-171) blocks only by exact match against BLOCKED_HOSTS and by ipaddress.ip_address parsing. Some host forms fail both checks and are accepted as ordinary hostnames, but the OS resolver used by httpx still maps them to the metadata address. Examples: http://2852039166/ (decimal for 169.254.169.254), http://0xa9fea9fe/, http://0251.254.169.254/, and http://metadata.google.internal./ (trailing dot). This gap is in the unchanged helper and validate_arr_url has the same gap, so it predates this diff; the diff just applies the helper to one more input. pending: confirm httpx/getaddrinfo in the deployed container resolves the decimal or trailing-dot forms to 169.254.169.254.
members.why_it_matters: The docstring promises that metadata addresses are blocked at config load, but alternate spellings of the same address get through.
members.fix_hint: in the helper, strip a trailing '.' from hostname and normalise or resolve numeric host forms (e.g. socket.inet_aton) before the BLOCKED_HOSTS and ip_address checks
members.current_code:
from triggarr.web.validation import validate_arr_url_config

ok, err = validate_arr_url_config(v)

members.title: New config-load SSRF validator inherits non-canonical IP literal bypass from shared helper
members.problem: The new field_validator wires InstanceConfig.url through triggarr.web.validation.validate_arr_url_config (unchanged in this diff). That helper's hostname check does ipaddress.ip_address(hostname) and, on ValueError, falls through to 'treat as DNS hostname, no further check'. Non-canonical IP literal encodings (trailing-dot 169.254.169.254., decimal-integer 2852039166, octal, hex) all raise ValueError from Python's strict ipaddress parser, so they bypass both the BLOCKED_HOSTS exact-string match and the ip_address()-based link-local/metadata checks. This is a pre-existing gap in the shared helper's logic (also present in validate_arr_url for the web-form path), not something introduced by this diff's own changed lines; before this diff config-load had no SSRF validation at all, so this is a net improvement.
source_window: Raises ValueError on violation so Pydantic surfaces a ValidationError.
members.why_it_matters: If the bypass is confirmed against the actual resolver in use, anyone who can write triggarr.toml could configure a *arr URL that resolves to the cloud-metadata address despite the new validator appearing to reject it.
members.fix_hint: in validate_arr_url[_config], after the ipaddress.ip_address() ValueError branch, re-check the raw hostname string for a trailing dot / all-digit / 0x-prefixed form and reject or normalize before treating it as an opaque DNS name

members.title: Metadata-host block can be bypassed with decimal or trailing-dot IP forms (gap in the existing helper, capped note)
members.problem: I ran validate_arr_url_config directly. 'http://2852039166:80' (decimal form of 169.254.169.254) and 'http://169.254.169.254.:80' (trailing dot) both return (True, ''). ipaddress.ip_address rejects both strings, and BLOCKED_HOSTS uses exact-string matching. getaddrinfo, used by httpx, resolves both to the metadata IP. This is in the unchanged helper logic; the strict validate_arr_url has the same gap, so this diff only extends an existing gap to one more caller.
